Report Comparison (client-safe): Hazira gas release and fire, 2020

The operator's HSE and engineering leads · Hazira 2020 · 2020-09-24 · run 2020-09-24-hazira-gas-release-fire · generated 2026-10-21

About 18 min read

Learning purposes: not a statutory document. Derived from a ProbeMatrix investigation export; learnings are evidence-linked but should be validated by the organisation before adoption. · Learnings drafted by an AI agent from AI-assisted findings

Review: draft · Classification: internal · Version 1.0

Draft because: the investigation status is in progress; no finding is marked as edited by a person

Data quality and limits

  • Draft learnings from an unreviewed analysis: the export's Investigation Status is in progress and no finding is marked as edited by a person.

Bottom line

  • Both analyses rest on the same evidence: the export was built from the enquiry committee's report, so this compares how each analysis organises the same facts.
  • The two agree closely: each of the 25 register learnings has a counterpart in the committee's report (21 at the same level, 4 in part), and 76 of its 84 items map to a learning (46 fully, 30 in part).
  • The register states the organisational reason for four conditions that the committee's report records as facts: independent checks on high-consequence repairs, repeat seal failures, the move from locating a leak to isolating it, and how warnings travelled to the control room.
  • The committee's recommendations are mostly procedural (25 of 35) with 8 engineering changes; the register's 44 recommendations include 20 engineering and 4 elimination or substitution changes.
  • The committee's report is more specific on plant engineering and testing detail, such as the fire-pump test regime, incident classification, logbooks and control-room layout.

Basis of the comparison

3

Comparison against the other report: Enquiry committee report on the major fire at the Hazira gas processing plant on 24.09.2020 (enquiry committee constituted by the national petroleum and natural gas regulator; regulator-constituted enquiry under an office order of 30.09.2020; the report does not name the statutory provision). The comparison covers analysis coverage, not the quality of either investigation.

Sighted comparison: 8 of the 46 evidence items behind the export quote or point to the committee's recommendations, and 92 of the 436 findings refer to them (a search of each finding's label, summary, justification and causal text for pages 34 to 36, a recommendation number such as B.5, or the committee recommending). The comparison therefore shows how the committee's facts read when they are sorted into learnings by organisational level; it is not a second investigation.

Evidence: direct

This comparison was written with the ProbeMatrix learnings coach. The match judgments are in comparison-map.json for the reader to check.

Where the other report is stronger

3

The committee's fire-fighting section is more specific: pump run frequency and capacity tests against the industry standard, diesel logs, maintenance split across departments, and the reporting line of the fire crews (OBS-15 to OBS-20, REC-11 to REC-16). The register covers the unavailable diesel pumps (LR-23) [; ].

It covers topics the register does not take up: incident classification and review (OBS-11, REC-07), logbooks and handover records (OBS-43, REC-35), control-room panel layout (REC-31) and storage of rubber spares (REC-27).

Its evidence is first-hand: the site inspection, eyewitness interviews, CCTV frames and control-room data, and several recommendations are direct plant changes, such as unique tags on every flameproof fitting (REC-24) and remote operation of all motor-operated valves (REC-03) [; ; ; ].

Limits of this comparison

3

The export was built from the committee's written report only, without site access, interviews or records, so its findings depend on the committee's account. The committee's report gives two different years for one seal change; the export follows the later one [; ].

The inventory of the committee's items was typed by hand from the report's text, with roles in place of names and functions in place of company names; recommendations were split by their sub-numbers. The control tiers of the committee's recommendations are this comparison's classification. Section 11's narrative conclusions and its reconstruction are not inventoried as separate items; its six numbered root causes stand for them.

Two findings quote recommendation text, numbered D.2.iii and D.2.iv, that the committee's report does not contain [; ]; this comparison uses the report's own wording.

Evidence trail

FND-23139BF9
No accountable owner or recorded authority for gasket material specification and procurement · L4 · rating 4. No organizational role owned the meter gasket specification, procurement quality control, or the authority to approve the substitution from OEM rectangular-slot gasket to locally procured O-ring.
FND-82FC718D
Recurring gasket failures on 310FT01 treated as routine maintenance instead of reliability warning · L4 · rating 4. Three gasket replacements in ~22 months did not trigger root-cause analysis or engineering correction; the same inadequate relining was repeated until the fourth failure.
FND-F8C125D5
Pressure-boundary maintenance ordered without independent QC/inspection manning · L3 · rating 4. The gasket replacement job was authorised without any independent QC, inspection, or permit-verification manning, leaving the substitute O-ring and omitted hydrotest wholly unchecked.
FND-36179046
Night-shift emergency response leadership — failure to establish immediate isolation plan (02:35–03:01) · L2 · rating 4. Night-shift leaders at the gate did not establish a shared urgent plan; MOV 54 was closed 26 minutes after their arrival and 46 minutes after detection.
FND-BC00FF3A
CISF perimeter notification path required CCTV Control Room verification hop before reaching operating control room · L2 · rating 3. CISF perimeter posts had no direct notification channel to the Gas Terminal Control Room; calls had to relay through the CCTV Control Room, adding roughly 3-5 minutes to initial notification.
FND-02310148
Emergency isolation MOVs never upgraded for remote operation from the control room · L4 · rating 4. MOV 54 and the gas-terminal MOVs remained local-manual with no emergency remote control, forcing physical attendance and delaying first isolation to 03:01 — 46 minutes after detection.
FND-A4B843EB
Fire-water diesel pump reliability degraded by outstanding maintenance · L2 · rating 2. Two of four fire-water diesel pumps were under maintenance and one was tripping after 2 minutes, leaving the diesel backup unreliable during the incident.
FND-8C0BB623
Maintenance Team - Gasket Replacement Without OEM Spec · L1 · rating 4. Maintenance team lacked technical knowledge to recognize that substituting unspecified O-rings for OEM rectangular-slot gaskets without hydrostatic testing created unacceptable pressure boundary risk.
FND-7A32AC87
Maintenance Team - Wrong Choice: Substitute O-ring for OEM Rectangular-Slot Gasket · L1 · rating 4. Maintenance team wrongly chose to use locally-sourced substitute O-rings without specification control instead of OEM rectangular-slot gaskets for meter 310FT01.
FND-89962239
Gasket replacement using non-standard material - 18 Sep 2020 · L1 · rating 4. Maintenance personnel used wrong gasket type (O-ring vs rectangular-slot) without specification or quality control, deviating fundamentally from correct replacement procedure.
FND-7C5ED5B3
Maintenance Team - Hydrostatic Test Requirement After Gasket Replacement · L1 · rating 4. Maintenance team unaware of or misapplied hydrostatic test requirement after pressure boundary work - pressurized to operating pressure only instead of design pressure validation.
FND-FD617187
Maintenance Team - No Hydro-Test Requirement Ignored · L1 · rating 4. Maintenance team skipped mandatory hydrostatic test after gasket replacement on 18-Sep-2020, ignoring fundamental pressure boundary integrity verification requirement.
FND-212DC9B7
Maintenance Team - No Hydrostatic Test After Gasket Replacement · L1 · rating 4. Maintenance team delayed/omitted mandatory hydrostatic test after gasket replacement on 18-Sep-2020, returning meter to service without pressure boundary validation.
FND-2FAB8D51
Maintenance job planning for the 18-Sep-2020 gasket replacement on 310FT01 · L2 · rating 4. The 18-Sep-2020 gasket job was planned without the OEM specification, part quality control, hydrostatic test, or notification closure — all critical preparatory elements failed.
FND-A6312B6B
Gasket replacement unverified maintenance process · L2 · rating 4. Gasket replacement had no independent quality checks: no material spec, no QC, no hydrotest, relying entirely on the fitter's execution.
FND-28F8790B
Maintenance material & quality verification roles not assigned · L2 · rating 4. No one was assigned to verify gasket specification, quality, or post-installation integrity, leaving quality control to individual discretion.

Maintenance Supervisors - SAP Notification Closure Procedure · L1 · rating 3. Maintenance supervisors unaware of or misapplied SAP notification closure procedure requiring review before return to service, allowing defective gasket work to proceed.

EVD-8645
document: Lost OEM gasket specification; market-sourced O-rings used as substitutes without QC. Source records: "The meter is very old (1986) and having rectangular slot for the gasket. Original Specifications of gasket are not available, and the gaskets were not being procured from the OEMs. Instead, use of locally purchased O ring was done in its place as a regular practice. There was no specification or quality control during the purchase of the O rings. There is no record of date or authority of the decision to switch over from OEM supplied gasket to locally purchased gasket" (p.31). Six omissions documented in two sentences: lost spec, no OEM procurement, market O-ring substitution, no specification, no quality control, no documented authorisation. The committee's root cause #2 ("Use of nonstandard O ring") and #3 ("Lack of control over material sourcing") flow directly from this finding. The same governance failure underlies the absence of MOC application across the plant since 2018 (row 47).
EVD-1494
document: Meter 310FE1 gasket replacement history. Source records: "Cleaning/servicing/calibration of meters 1 & 2 was carried out on 12th & 13th Nov 2018. Afterwards, meter no.1 was cleaned on 25/02/2019 & gasket was changed. Again on 18/09/2019, gasket was changed which leaked within one year" (p.27). [Note: source references 18/09/2019 in the text but 18/09/2020 in the contextual narrative on p.31; the 2020 date is the most-recent gasket change.] Three gasket replacements in ~22 months on a 1986-vintage meter with 34 years in service: 12-Nov-2018, 25-Feb-2019, 18-Sep-2020. Recurrent sealing issues visible in the SAP record; the pattern did not trigger material/procedure review and the same locally-sourced O-ring continued in use (row 30).
EVD-2432
log_record: Fire Water System monitoring record during incident response. Source records: "Both the Tank level and the Fire water header pressure were healthy throughout the incident. Three electrical Fire water pumps namely 47PE003 A, C, D were operated during the cooling activity" (p.11). FW availability was adequate during this incident. However, latent issue flagged by the committee (p.27): "Out of 4 diesel pumps 410 m3/hr, 2 pumps are under maintenance, one operated for 30 minutes & fourth pumps is tripping after 2 minutes. The reason for tripping is not identified or actions have not been recorded." Three of four diesel pumps had maintenance or reliability issues; only electrical pumps carried this incident. Had cooling demand been higher or had electrical supply failed, the response would have been constrained.
EVD-0185
log_record: Meter 310FE1 returned to service ~46 hours after the 18-Sep-2020 gasket replacement. Source records: "Next day meter 310FE01 was taken on online and was in use at the time of Incident" (p.31). Replacement on 18-Sep; back online 19-Sep; in service through to incident (24-Sep). No post-maintenance pressure validation captured (row 32). SAP notification 3800419840 not closed after job completion (row 28). The committee recommendation D.2.ii at p.35 explicitly addresses the closure-review gap: "Sample checks/approval of closure of notifications by Senior Officers to be introduced".
EVD-2506
log_record: Calibration record showing undocumented setting change on meter 310FT01 in Dec 2019. Source records: "During calibration from 17/12/2019 to 18/12/2019, calibration was changed from 16000 mmwc to 2540 mmwc for 310FT01 without any mention of this change in the calibration documents signed by the team. During next calibration for meter 310FT01 was again changed to 16000 MMWC. No checklist is followed while carrying such critical jobs of high pressure/risk" (p.27). Setting changed 16000 -> 2540 mmwc (~6.3x reduction), then reversed to 16000 mmwc on next cycle, with neither change recorded in the signed calibration document. No checklist used for the high-pressure work. The committee recommendation D.1.i (p.35) explicitly addresses this gap: "details of Master calibrator/action taken/replacement/deviation from procedure if any, is to be documented in the calibration certificate".
EVD-5634
document: Control Room Training Program — 4-day general training, no defined qualification, no simulator. Source records: "control room operations are carried out by persons inadequately trained in safety, operations, control room handling, logbook records and actions during emergency. It is informed that four days training programme is conducted for new recruitment/transfer staff which is general in nature and later the job training is carried out. Qualification of this staff is also not defined in HR/Operations Policy. Most of the staff have attended only One Basic Course since 2018" (p.30). The committee recommends (p.36): "operating staffs of control room needs to be trained for at least 1 month (preferably on simulators) before being assigning Control Room duties enabling them to handle operations & emergencies effectively" — a near-eightfold expansion of the current 4-day initial training. Three documented gaps: short initial training, no defined qualification in HR/Operations Policy, no simulator-based emergency training.
EVD-9692
document: Self Safety Audit (SSA) Report — generic checklist not tailored to plant specifics. Source records: "Safety self-audit is conducted by a multi-disciplinary team based on the checklist prepared by the location. The checklist is comprehensive but not related to specific plants and in the process, lot of observations are missing. The duration of audit is not indicated and in most of the items, compliances are indicated, but during our inspection, the data is found to be incomplete & not in line with OISD standards/manuals. Approved manuals/SOPs were not available" (p.26). Three documented gaps: checklist not plant-specific, duration not indicated, compliance claims unverified. The committee's recommendation B.1 at p.34 calls for "Checklist for Self-Safety Audit for individual plants are to be developed" — implying the audit instrument itself was not fit for purpose.
EVD-3452
document: Plant layout drawings reviewed by the committee, including main plant layout and Flame & Gas detector overlay. Source records the document set: "Layout of the Plant / Layout of Plant along with F&G detectors / Layout of MCP-Gas Terminal" (p.18). F&G detection coverage exists per drawing. The critical operational implication is found at p.26: "F&G detection system does not have provision for auto shut down of plant or activation of fire suppression system" — the coverage is documented and instrumented but not interlocked to action. The committee's recommendation A.1 at p.34 explicitly calls for: "F&G detection system needs to be interlocked to automatic plant shut down and activation of fire suppression system." This is the same gap that allowed the 46-minute pre-ignition response delay.
EVD-0210
photograph: Photograph of the watch tower and CCTV camera mounting position relative to the damaged area. Source identifies the camera: "PELCO make PTZ cameras (Model D5230D) are provided at few places and has turn around (360 degree) at the time of about 90 seconds. Visibility from this camera is limited" (p.30). The photograph documents the physical layout that produced the design constraint — a single PTZ camera with ~90 s pan cycle is the sole video coverage for the metering skid + GT CR area, and its destruction with the cable at 03:08:22 (row 13) terminated the evidence chain. The committee recommends per-plant CCTV with master-control/CISF display (p.36).
EVD-2752
recording: CCTV frame 03:08:22 — source describes as "major fire continued, CCTV capturing discontinued due to burnt of CCTV cable" (p.25). Hard cutoff for the video evidence timeline, 7 seconds after ignition. The cable's exposure to fire-temperature was sufficient to terminate recording inside one camera's view. The committee's subsequent recommendation (p.36) — "CCTV arrangement shall be provided for each plant including separately with display at plant control rooms as well as master control/CISF station" — acknowledges that a single PELCO PTZ D5230D camera (~90s pan, p.30) was the sole video coverage for this critical area, and its loss with the cable destroyed the evidence chain at the transition from pre-ignition to post-ignition.
EVD-5105
document: Work Permit / Job Safety Plan (JSA) system — missing permits without tracking. Source records: "Work Permits are issued in SAP and hard copy of work permits are at sites during execution of work. After completion of work, the originals are filed. On checking the same, it was found that few of the work permits were missing. No data is kept on such missing permits. Job safety Plan is not attached/given in SAP document. Closing of permits & actions indicated in work needs review" (p.26). Multiple gaps: missing original permits with no log of which are missing, JSPs absent from SAP for non-routine/hazardous work, permit closure not reviewed. The committee's recommendation B.5 at p.34 notes: "Maintenance notifications are not be assumed as permit to work" — implying that maintenance work was being executed under SAP notifications without separate work-permit authorisation. Permit lifecycle not auditable.
EVD-2894
document: Pressure boundary integrity record: NO hydro test performed after 18-Sep-2020 gasket replacement. Source records: "After calibration of the meter 310FE01, the gasket was replaced on 18.09.2020. No hydro test was done after replacement of the gasket. The system was only pressurised to operating pressure (Both meters were in line) and isolated. Next day meter 310FE01 was taken on online and was in use at the time of Incident" (p.31). System pressurised only to operating pressure; standard pressure-boundary integrity test (hydro test to design pressure) not performed. The committee directly cites this as a contributing cause: "Probable cause of leak is due to use of nonstandard gasket and not testing the system to designed pressure. No standard operating procedure is in place for calibration and taking back in service of these meters which are operating at high pressures" (p.32).
EVD-0591
log_record: SAP Notification 3800419840 raised 17-Sep-2020 for malfunction of meter 310FE1 / 310FT01. Source records: "Notification no. 3800419840 was raised on 17/09/2020 for malfunction of meter no.1" (p.27); confirmed p.33: "SAP Notification 3800419840 dt. 17.09.2020 was raised for checking meter 1." Sequence: 14-17 Sep performance check observed jerks from meter 1; notification raised 17-Sep; gasket replaced 18-Sep; meter back online 19-Sep; incident 24-Sep. The actionable maintenance trigger preceded the incident by exactly 7 days. The corrective work executed (gasket replacement using locally-sourced O-ring without specification or QC, see row 30) was inadequate to address the underlying issue. The notification "was not closed after completion of the job" (p.27) — no supervisory closure check.
EVD-2986
document: Management of Change (MOC) SOP published Aug 2016 — not implemented since 2018. Source records: "Management of Change (MOC) philosophy/SOP was published in August 2016. However, the procedure indicated in the document is not implemented while carrying out change of Low-Pressure Gas to Kribhico from Medium Pressure Gas headers in LPG Plant in 2013 & 2018. It is informed no more MOCs are implemented in the plant since 2018" (p.30). MOC SOP exists since Aug 2016. Two named uncovered changes: LP gas to Kribhico from MP headers in 2013 and 2018. ZERO MOCs issued at all since 2018 — the SOP is a paper artefact, not an active control. The same governance failure underlies the undocumented gasket substitution at the metering skid (row 30: "There is no record of date or authority of the decision to switch over from OEM supplied gasket to locally purchased gasket"). Published policy not applied in practice.
EVD-4052
document: On-site Disaster Management Plan (DMP) — hydrocarbon-leakage section omits isolation/stoppage decision criteria. Source records: "As per DMP On site Hazira Plant, guidelines to be followed in case of hydrocarbon leakage are included but does not include isolation/stoppage of facilities/pipelines" (p.32). Reinforced at p.27: "In ERDMP, scenario for Level 3 emergencies are taken from the plant failures. Heavy product/gas leakages from pipelines & tanks are considered but decision on isolation/closure of plant/pipelines is not mentioned." The DMP defines the scenario but not the decision: when does a hydrocarbon leak warrant unilateral pipeline isolation, and who has the authority to call it? This procedural gap directly correlates with the 46-minute response delay — personnel had no documented criterion to act on, and authority was concentrated above the shift-in-charge level (row 50). The committee's root cause #6 ("Non isolation/stoppage of 36 pipeline operation") flows from this finding.
EVD-9612
witness_statement: Witness statement of DGM (Production) - GSP Shift In-charge, called from quarters at ~02:35 hrs. Source records: "At around 0235 hrs, [DGM-GSP] received phone call from LPG Control Room and Gas Terminal control room, it was informed that heavy gas leakage near 36 metering area... [he] tried to enter the Gas Control room area but could not enter due to heavy gas smell. He informed Fire station to abstain from any vehicle movement in the plant... Further [DGM-GSP] closed the MOV 54 inlet condensate line from slug catcher to 36 metering area at about 0301 hrs. Thereafter fire occurred." (p.17). MOV 54 closure at 03:01 is 46 minutes after first physical detection (02:15) and 7 minutes before ignition (03:08:15). The shift in-charge had to physically reach Gas Terminal Gate before he could close the valve — the MOVs in the gas terminal station are not remote-operable from the control room during emergency (p.26).
EVD-3932
document: Plant organogram — night-shift authority chain reconstructed from witness statements (rows 1-7) and the committee's document review (p.18). Authority chain: perimeter (CISF Constable A) -> CCTV CR (CISF SI C) -> Gas Terminal CR (CE-P) -> GSP/LPG Shift In-charge (DGM-P) -> Overall Shift In-charge / SIC (GM-P) -> Resident Engineer (GM-P) + Head Operations (CGM-P) -> Plant Manager / CIC (GGM). Critical structural observation: NO role between Shift In-charge and Plant Manager has standing authority to close MOV 54 (or any other emergency-isolation valve) without telephoning up the chain — confirmed by the committee finding (p.26) that "MOVs are provided in the gas terminal station for local operations but they are not having remote operation from control room during emergency." The Overall Shift In-charge had to physically reach Gas Terminal Gate at ~02:35 and then "instructed closure" (row 7) — the operator at Gas Terminal Gate could not act unilaterally. Directly implicates the 46-minute first-detection-to-first-isolation gap. The escalation hierarchy was not designed for time-critical hydrocarbon containment.
EVD-8657
log_record: DCS annunciator panel record showing first alarm activation at the Gas Terminal Control Room at ~02:20 hrs. Source records: "At around 0220 hrs Mr. [CE] heard alarm on the annunciator panel" (p.17). Quantitative comparison: leak onset 02:12:50 (CCTV) -> human detection 02:15 (CISF) -> annunciator alarm 02:20. The automated detection lagged human detection by 5 minutes and lagged leak onset by ~7 minutes 10 seconds. The committee notes (p.26): "Hydrocarbon/H2S detectors are configured to Annunciator Panel for display but not in DCS for history" and "F&G detection system does not have provision for auto shut down of plant or activation of fire suppression system." The detector data is configured for display-only, not for trend/predictive alarms or auto-isolation interlocks.
EVD-6916
physical_item: HPMV (high-pressure mercury vapour) flame-proof lamp post with compromised integrity, identified by the committee as the probable ignition source. Source records: "three bolts on one of the flame proof lamps were missing resulting in it being open with its integrity compromised, glass case got detached from the main body and had opened out about 5 to 6 cms. The nearby fittings were found intact" (p.32). Three bolts missing; glass case opened 5-6 cm. The "nearby fittings were intact" qualifier bounds the ignition origin to this single lamp. The Zone 1 hydrocarbon area requires flame-proof integrity; that integrity was demonstrably absent on this fitting.
EVD-4286
witness_statement: Witness statement of CISF Constable A on duty at Watch Tower 3 (NW periphery) since 21:00 hrs. Source records: "At 0215 hrs, he observed noise followed by vapour cloud from Gas Terminal Area" (p.16); he then informed CISF Main Gate, Fire Station, and Main LPG Control Room. First physical detection of the leak event - approximately 145 seconds after CCTV-confirmed leak onset at 02:12:50, and ~5 minutes before the operating-area annunciator alarm at 02:20. Critical observation: the detection came from perimeter security, not from the on-shift operating personnel near the source.
EVD-6470
log_record: Pressure Transmitter Data MISSING for 310PT4, 310PT5, 310PT6. Source records: "Three Pressure transmitters 310PT4, 310PT5 & 310PT6 are shown in the drawing. It was informed that no pressure transmitter data are available in the system. No pressure data in Gas Terminal area is available/provided to check rise in pressure in the metering lines" (p.26). Three transmitters shown in P&ID; zero pressure data retained for the pre-incident window. Significant data-retention / DCS-configuration governance gap. Pre-incident pressure trend on the metering lines could have anchored the leak detection earlier than 02:15 (perimeter) or 02:20 (annunciator); its absence impaired both real-time alarm and forensic reconstruction.
EVD-5527
document: 2017 thickness analysis report identifying pipes with significant thickness loss. Source records: "As per the report of 2017, several pipes have been identified with significant thickness loss and need for corrective action. However, even after three years no plan has been developed for the corrective actions to be taken for those lines. Mere measurement of thickness without corrective action does not complete the process of maintaining the integrity of pipes" (p.30). 3+ year gap from 2017 finding to 24-Sep-2020 incident; zero corrective action plan developed in that window. The committee's direct phrasing — "Mere measurement of thickness without corrective action does not complete the process" — is an explicit organisational-process finding: recommendations issued without follow-up enforcement, known thickness losses unaddressed.
EVD-8307
document: Ultrasonic Thickness (UT) pipeline measurement records for the gas-terminal area. Source records: "The laid down schedule for thickness measurement is every four years... As per the records, the last two thickness measurement exercise was carried out in 2011 and 2017 which suggests that the schedule of four years is not being adhered to strictly" (p.29). Mandated cycle: 4 years; actual gap 2011 -> 2017 = 6 years; gap 2017 -> 24-Sep-2020 = 3+ years. Two compliance failures: the 4-year cycle was breached, and the post-2017 follow-up never occurred. Integrity-management precondition: pipe thickness not characterised within mandated window.
EVD-0933
document: P&ID Drawing 02-310-AO-101 Rev.1 covering the 2x6" lines and 1x2" line metering system. Source records: "Reference drawings no. 02-310-AO-101 Rev.1, 2x6 lines & 1x2 lines for metering system are shown but valves & meters configuration are not matching. As old drawings were lost, new drawings are made by a vendor but the same has not been checked & approved by ONGC" (p.26). Three governance failures documented: original drawings lost, vendor-prepared replacement not approved by operator, and field-installation configuration does not match the unapproved drawing. The drawing exists nominally but is not a controlled engineering document. The same governance gap underlies the F&G interlock absence and the missing PT-data observation (row 26). As-built drawings not maintained; configuration management absent.
EVD-6852
document: External Safety Audit Report Feb 2018 — 12 of 308 recommendations overdue without documented authority. Source records: "External safety audit was conducted in February 2018, and 296 out of 308 recommendations are complied with. Balance are in various stages and dates are extended till 30/04/2021. Document indicating approval from Director Offshore for extending the target date was not available as per the procedure" (p.26). 308 total recommendations; 296 complied (96%); 12 outstanding with extensions to 30-Apr-2021. The critical control failure is not the 12 outstanding items but the absence of competent-authority approval for the extensions — the procedure exists but was not followed for the extension authorisation.
EVD-2130
log_record: Monthly fire drill records in SAP — lacking action/observation data. Source records: "Fire drill reports are available in SAP but without any data on actions taken/recommendations. Separate data is maintained which is not in line with the approved guidelines" (p.26). Two parallel records: SAP (incomplete — dates only, no actions or observations) and a separate informal data set (not approved-guidelines compliant). Drill effectiveness cannot be measured from either record. Documentation discipline weak; emergency-response readiness not evidence-based.
EVD-1460
witness_statement: Witness statement of Chief Engineer (Production), Gas Terminal CR, on night shift from 20:00 hrs. Source records: "At around 0220 hrs Mr. [CE] heard alarm on the annunciator panel and the same time he received a phone call from CISF SI [CCTV CR] from CCTV Control room informing him about some vapour cloud or steam leakage in Gas Terminal PH I area" (p.17). On going outside the control room he "saw the heavy cloud in phase I area" but could not approach due to dense cloud. He then informed GSP Shift I/C, LPG Shift I/C, and CFU Panel Engineer. The vapour cloud was already opaque enough by 02:20 to deny on-foot inspection of the source area. The annunciator alarm at 02:20 lagged human detection by 5 minutes — the automated detection did not pre-empt operator notification.
EVD-9220
witness_statement: Witness statement of Junior Engineer (Mechanical), Gas Terminal CR, on night shift from 20:00 hrs. Source records: "At 0220 hrs Mr. [JEA] heard alarm and phone call simultaneously. He went out of the control room and observed leakage and intense smell from Phase-I area. Visibility was very poor" (p.17). The witness joined the in-progress response rather than initiating a parallel one. Documents that secondary detection by on-shift operating personnel lagged primary CISF perimeter detection by ~5 minutes despite the witness being closer to the source. Visibility was poor enough by 02:20 to limit on-foot inspection.
EVD-0496
photograph: Post-incident electrical PM audit photographs of 9 HPMV FLP lamps (125 W each) in the metering-skid blast radius. Source describes the audit report itself: "the report has clubbed all nine 125 W HPMV FLP lamps together and reported 'cable burnt and fitting damaged due to heat' as status for all of them. However, the unique condition of one particular lamp due to the type of damage suffered by it with respect to its area of installation was not mentioned in the report" (p.28). The committee further notes "the electrical maintenance system is a lot more skewed towards breakdown maintenance and lays little emphasis on systematic preventive maintenance and inspection" (p.28). 9 of 9 fittings showed cable/fitting damage; one (row 16) had pre-existing integrity loss (3 missing bolts, glass case opened 5-6 cm) — a uniform deterioration pattern not consistent with single-event fire damage alone, indicating a systemic gap in PM coverage for FLP fittings in Zone 1/2 areas.
